findings.reason: At apply.js:52-63 the loop breaks after the first marker, so for '-b', '\', '+c', '\' only addEOFNL is set and line 70-72 pushes '' (the result gains '\n'). With '+' first, only removeEOFNL is set and line 67 returns false at fuzzFactor 0. The diff removes the old `if (addEOFNL)` branch inside `if (removeEOFNL)` that handled this case, so the earlier 'do nothing' behaviour is gone.
findings.claim: The new `break` stops the EOF-marker scan at the first '\ No newline at end of file'. The diff also deletes the branch for the both-markers case. Together these mean that changing an unterminated final line now adds a trailing newline, or rejects a valid patch, depending on the order of the -/+ lines.
findings.evidence:
In the loop at lines 52-63, a standard hunk such as `-b`, `\ No newline at end of file`, `+c`, `\ No newline at end of file` reaches the first marker after the '-' line. That sets `addEOFNL = true` and then hits `break`, so `removeEOFNL` is never set by the second marker. Control then reaches `else if (addEOFNL)` (line 70). For source 'a
b' the last element is 'b' (not ''), so `lines.push('')` runs and the final `resultLines.join('
')` returns 'a
c
' instead of 'a
c'. Before the change, both flags were set and this case was handled as 'do nothing'.
